column4: Modernizing Government Regulations (MGR) for National Competitiveness and Productivity
column6:
The MGR Program aims to contribute in creating a conducive environment for businesses to develop and grow by enhancing market competition for businesses, strengthening engagement and advocacy of the citizens, and strengthening the regulatory capacity and governance of the government. To advance these aims, the MGR Program continues to assess the existing regulatory environments of priority industries and sectors (i.e., identifying how current rules influence business growth, citizen experience, and government performance) and develops reform proposals to make regulations more relevant, coherent, and supportive of national development through its four components:

1. Program Management Component provides overall leadership and coordination of the MGRP across government agencies. It supports the institutionalization of the Regulatory Quality Management System (RQMS) by developing a comprehensive implementation package, including standards, tools, procedures, and capacity-building modules—to guide agencies in establishing and sustaining strong regulatory management systems. Program Management also oversees strategic planning, monitoring, reporting, and alignment with national priorities.

2. Regulatory Review Component conducts systematic post-implementation reviews of problematic regulations affecting priority industries and sectors. Through evidence-based analysis, it identifies regulatory burdens, inefficiencies, overlaps, and outdated provisions. The findings are translated into actionable recommendations to streamline processes, reduce compliance costs, and improve regulatory coherence and effectiveness across government.

3. Capacity Development enhances the technical capabilities of regulatory agencies to design and implement high-quality regulations. Major initiatives under this component include: a) piloting the RQMS in four identified agencies to test, refine, and demonstrate its application in real regulatory environments, b)roviding targeted technical assistance to both local government units (LGUs) and national government agencies (NGAs) through the Regulatory Impact Assesment (RIA) Clinic, offering hands-on support across all stages of the RIA process, c) developing a Regulatory Competency Framework that defines the skills, knowledge, and behavioral competencies required of modern regulators to ensure professionalism and consistency across the regulatory workforce.

4. Advocacy Component promotes transparency, stakeholder engagement, and the institutionalization of good regulatory practices. Advocacy efforts focus on creating platforms for policy dialogue and knowledge exchange to refine and advance the recommendations emerging from the Program’s regulatory reviews. The goal is to transform these recommendations into actionable policies that can be readily adopted by concerned agencies or sectors. Initiatives include publications, policy briefs, multi-stakeholder discussions, and dissemination activities to strengthen buy-in and support for regulatory reform.

column4: Improve LGU Competitiveness and Ease of Doing Business (EODB)
column5: Department of the Interior and Local Government
column6:
The DILG continues to pursue its initiatives and advocacies on promoting the ease of doing business to promote local economic development pursuant to Republic Act No. 11032 or the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery (EODB-EGSD) Act of 2018, Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028 specifically on Chapter 10: Promote Competition and Improve Regulatory Efficiency, and the 8-Point Socioeconomic Agenda of the Marcos Administration on ensuring sound macroeconomic fundamentals through efficient and sound fiscal management, resilient, and innovative financial sector and advanced digital economy.

The EODB Program aims to reinvigorate the local business environment for economic growth; create local enabling environment to encourage local investments; improve LGU regulatory services through the adoption of digitalization and public services; and encourage private sector investments in public sector infrastructure and services toward local economic development.

The Cooperative Regulation Program (CRP) is CDA’s primary regulatory initiative to ensure cooperatives operate in compliance with the Cooperative Code, related laws, and CDA rules. As the sole agency granting juridical personality through the Certificate of Registration (COR), CDA requires cooperatives to secure a Certificate of Compliance (COC) via mandatory reports and periodic on-site inspections.
Inspections, examinations, and investigations provide the basis for regulatory or developmental interventions, ensuring cooperatives uphold accountability, transparency, and lawful operations. The program also protects cooperatives from abuse of legal privileges by enforcing compliance, and when necessary, canceling or delisting erring cooperatives.

Key regulatory services under CRP include:
•	Registration of cooperatives and amendments
•	Formulation of guidelines and regulatory standards
•	Validation and verification of proposed cooperatives
•	Pre-Membership Education Seminars
•	Nationwide inspection and classification of cooperatives (micro, small, medium, large)
•	Examination and investigation of cooperatives
•	Capacity-building for mandatory report preparation
•	Issuance of notices for cooperatives under Dissolution, Liquidation, Cancellation, and Delisting (DLCD)

Ongoing PAPs include:
•	Electronic Cooperative Clinique Program
•	Regulation, Monitoring, and Supervision of Credit Surety Fund (CSF) Cooperatives
•	Registration and amendment services
•	Formulation of guidelines, rules, and regulations

The CRP ensures orderly, accountable, and sustainable cooperative operations, strengthening the sector as a credible instrument for social and economic development.

column4: Institutionalize Regulatory Management System and EODB Reforms
column6:
The Anti-Red Tape Authority is mandated to coordinate with all government offices covered under Section 3 of RA11032 in the review of existing laws, executive issuances and local ordinances, and recommend the repeal of the same if deemed outdated, redundant, and adds undue regulatory burden to the transacting public.

In 2020, ARTA launched the National Effort for the Harmonization of Efficient Measures of Inter-related Agencies (NEHEMIA) Program with an overall goal of reducing the time, cost, requirements, and procedures of transacting with the government using the whole-of-government approach in the sectors of Food and Pharmaceutical, Housing, Telecommunications, Energy, and Logistics. Additional priority sectors, i.e., Water, Responsible Mining, and Agriculture, were included in the Program in 2024.

The e-Kalasag project is an expanded initiative to better fulfill the mandate of the DTI to protect consumers and legitimate businesses, and to intensify the Department's activities and programs on monitoring, surveillance, enforcement, prosecution and adjudication including execution of decisions relevant to trade and industry laws, rules and regulations, as well as the conduct of quick response actions during periods of calamities, disasters and public emergencies.
